form.current-chamber: IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES

action.action-desc: Mr. Wicker (for himself, Mrs. Capito, Mr. Moran, Mr. Young, Mrs. Blackburn, Mr. Thune, Mr. Sullivan, Ms. Cantwell, and Mr. Peters) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation
Reported by Ms. Cantwell, with an amendment
action.action-instruction: Omit the part struck through and insert the part printed in italic

form.official-title: To improve the efficient movement of freight at ports in the United States, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Facilitating Relief for Efficient Intermodal Gateways to Handle Transportation Act or the FREIGHT Act.

paragraph.text: The term Commission means the Federal Maritime Commission.
The term Secretary means the Secretary of Transportation.

section.header: Grant program to improve movement of freight

subsection.text: In this section:

paragraph.text: The term eligible entity means—

subparagraph.text: a port authority;
a State entity; and
a local entity.

paragraph.text: The term program means the discretionary grant program established under subsection (b).

subsection.text: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall establish, within the Office of the Secretary, a discretionary grant program relating to improving the efficient movement of freight at ports.
The goals of the program shall be to fund, through the provision of 1 or more grants, planning projects that—

paragraph.text: identify what would be needed for eligible entities—

subparagraph.text: to standardize the definitions of terms used in port operations and related documentation, including—

clause.text: terms used in bills of lading;
the terms used to identify various port call processes; and
terms used to notify relevant stakeholders that the freight of those stakeholders is available; or

subparagraph.text: to develop the technology needed to improve communication of eligible entities with respect to freight location, availability, and equipment among—

clause.text: port authorities;
marine terminal operators;
shippers;
rail carriers;
motor carriers and drayage providers; and
other relevant stakeholders; and

paragraph.text: result in a planning document described in subsection (e).

subsection.text: To be eligible to receive a grant under the program, an eligible entity shall submit to the Secretary an application, at such time, in such manner, and containing such information as the Secretary may require, including a description of the means by which the eligible entity will incorporate the views and input of other port stakeholders in identifying what would be needed to standardize the definitions described in subsection (c)(1)(A) and develop the technology described in subsection (c)(1)(B).
Each eligible entity that receives a grant under the program shall develop and submit to the Secretary, at such time as the Secretary determines to be appropriate, a planning document that—

paragraph.text: identifies what would be necessary to standardize the applicable definitions;
identifies what would be necessary to develop the applicable technology;

includes input from relevant stakeholders, such as marine terminal operators, port authorities, State and local governments, ocean carriers, barge operators, motor carriers, rail carriers, drayage providers, chassis providers, and freight forwarders and brokers; and
addresses concerns regarding data privacy.
The Federal share of the total costs of a project for which a grant is provided under the program shall be not more than 50 percent.
The maximum amount of a grant provided under the program shall be $1,000,000.
A grant provided under the program may be used for eligible project expenses, including—

subparagraph.text: communications hardware and software;
data management hardware and software; and
planning and engineering costs.

subsection.text: At the request of an eligible entity that receives a grant under the program, the Secretary shall provide to the eligible entity information relating to other grant programs offered through the Department of Transportation under which the planning projects of the eligible entity under the program may be considered to be an eligible activity.
The Secretary shall—

paragraph.text: analyze the information contained in each planning document submitted under subsection (e); and
develop and make publicly available lessons learned with respect to standardizing port definitions and communications technology based on that information.

subsection.text: There is authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary to carry out this section $2,500,000 for fiscal year 2023.

section.header: Study on documentation and terms used in freight transportation
section.text: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall enter into an agreement with the National Academy of Sciences under which the National Academy of Sciences shall carry out a study—

paragraph.text: to identify and document—

subparagraph.text: the documentation, the data and information exchange, and other actions necessary to transport freight from a point of origin overseas to a destination in the United States, or from a point of origin in the United States to a destination overseas, including transportation of the freight—

clause.text: from the point of origin to an ocean carrier;
on an ocean carrier;
through any port; and
by rail or truck from a port to the destination;

subparagraph.text: whether and how the key terms used in that documentation or the data and information exchanged, or to describe various actions to move freight, vary depending on—

clause.text: the type of freight being moved;
the mode by which the freight moves;
whether the freight is required to be moved by multiple modes;
the State or region in the United States from, through, or to which the freight moves;
the port or marine terminal operator;
the origination or destination of the freight; and
other relevant criteria; and

subparagraph.text: recommendations with respect to means to rationalize existing terms, documentation, and data and information exchanged to enable port stakeholders to better track and manage freight transfer and delivery; and

paragraph.text: to assess and determine—

subparagraph.text: the data held and shared across existing, separate data systems used in international transportation across different modes of transportation, with respect to methods to link those data across the existing, separate data systems;
the best methods to link and enable effective exchange of those data across existing systems, both domestically and internationally;
methods to standardize data obtained from long-standing separate data systems; and
gaps in existing data and technology standards that would be necessary to address the development of systems to allow port stakeholders to better track and predict—

clause.text: the location of freight at ports;
the availability of freight for pickup; and
the ability to receive and return equipment at ports.

subsection.text: In this section:

paragraph.text: The term Director means the Director of the Bureau of Transportation Statistics.
The term dwell time, with respect to a piece of equipment, means the quantity of time during which the piece of equipment is—

subparagraph.text: subject to maintenance; or
in use.

paragraph.text: The term marine container means an intermodal container with a length of—

subparagraph.text: not less than 20 feet; and
not greater than 45 feet.

paragraph.text: Each port, marine terminal operator, and chassis provider shall submit to the Director such data as the Director determines to be necessary for the implementation of this section, subject to subchapter III of chapter 35 of title 44, United States Code.
The Director of the Office of Management and Budget shall approve an information collection for purposes of this section by not later than 60 days after the date of enactment of this Act.

subsection.text: Not later than 240 days after the date of enactment of this Act, and not less frequently than monthly thereafter, the Director shall publish statistics relating to the dwell time of equipment used in intermodal transportation, including—

paragraph.text: total dwell time, from all causes, of marine containers and marine container chassis; and
at a minimum, maintenance dwell time and in-use dwell time of marine containers and marine container chassis.

subsection.text: To the maximum extent practicable, the Director shall publish the statistics described in subsection (c)—

paragraph.text: on a local, regional, and national basis; and
at major coastal and inland port facilities.

subsection.text: The Chairperson of the Commission shall—

paragraph.text: establish on the public website of the Commission a webpage that allows for the submission of comments, complaints, concerns, reports of noncompliance, requests for investigation, and requests for alternative dispute resolution; and
direct each submission under the link established under paragraph (1) to the appropriate component office of the Commission.

subsection.header: Authorization of Office of Consumer Affairs and Dispute Resolution Services
subsection.text: The Commission shall maintain an Office of Consumer Affairs and Dispute Resolution Services to provide nonadjudicative ombuds assistance, mediation, facilitation, and arbitration to resolve challenges and disputes involving cargo shipments, household good shipments, and cruises subject to the jurisdiction of the Commission.

paragraph.text: Pursuant to section 41302 of title 46, United States Code, not later than 18 months after the date of enactment of this Act, the Chairperson of the Commission shall staff within the Bureau of Enforcement, the Bureau of Certification and Licensing, the Office of the Managing Director, the Office of Consumer Affairs and Dispute Resolution Services, and the Bureau of Trade Analysis not fewer than 7 total positions to assist in investigations and oversight, in addition to the positions within the Bureau of Enforcement, the Bureau of Certification and Licensing, the Office of the Managing Director, the Office of Consumer Affairs and Dispute Resolution Services, and the Bureau of Trade Analysis on that date of enactment.
The additional staff appointed under paragraph (1) shall provide support—

subparagraph.text: to Area Representatives of the Bureau of Enforcement;
to attorneys of the Bureau of Enforcement in enforcing the laws and regulations subject to the jurisdiction of the Commission;
for the alternative dispute resolution services of the Commission; or
for the review of agreements and activities subject to the authority of the Commission.

subsection.text: Not later than April 1, 2023, the Commission shall enter into an agreement with the Transportation Research Board of the National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine under which the Transportation Research Board shall carry out a study and develop best practices for on-terminal or near-terminal chassis pools that provide service to marine terminal operators, motor carriers, railroads, and other stakeholders that use the chassis pools, with the goal of optimizing supply chain efficiency and effectiveness.
In developing best practices under subsection (a), the Transportation Research Board shall—

paragraph.text: take into consideration—

subparagraph.text: practical obstacles to the implementation of chassis pools; and
potential solutions to those obstacles; and

paragraph.text: address relevant communication practices, information sharing, and knowledge management.

subsection.text: The Commission shall publish the best practices developed under this section on a publicly available website by not later than April 1, 2024.
There is authorized to be appropriated to the Commission to carry out this section $500,000.
Section 41102 of title 46, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following:
A common carrier, marine terminal operator, or ocean transportation intermediary, acting alone or in conjunction with any other person, directly or indirectly, may not—

paragraph.text: retaliate against a shipper, an agent of a shipper, an ocean transportation intermediary, or a motor carrier by refusing, or threatening to refuse, an otherwise-available cargo space accommodation; or
resort to any other unfair or unjustly discriminatory action for—

subparagraph.text: the reason that a shipper, an agent of a shipper, an ocean transportation intermediary, or motor carrier has—

clause.text: patronized another carrier; or
filed a complaint against the common carrier, marine terminal operator, or ocean transportation intermediary; or

subparagraph.text: any other reason.

subsection.text: Until a matter is referred to the Attorney General, the Federal Maritime Commission may—

paragraph.text: after notice and opportunity for a hearing, in accordance with this part—

subparagraph.text: assess a civil penalty; or

in addition to, or in lieu of, assessing a civil penalty under subparagraph (A), order a refund of money (including additional amounts in accordance with section 41305(c)), subject to subsection (b)(2); and

paragraph.text: compromise, modify, or remit, with or without conditions, a civil penalty or refund imposed under paragraph (1).
In determining the amount of a civil penalty assessed or refund of money ordered pursuant to subsection (a), the Federal Maritime Commission shall take into consideration—

subparagraph.text: the nature, circumstances, extent, and gravity of the violation committed;
with respect to the violator—

clause.text: the degree of culpability;
any history of prior offenses;
the ability to pay; and

In any case in which the Federal Maritime Commission orders a refund of money pursuant to subsection (a)(1)(B) in addition to assessing a civil penalty pursuant to subsection (a)(1)(A), the amount of the civil penalty assessed shall be decreased by any additional amounts included in the refund of money in excess of the actual injury (as defined in section 41305(a)).
A refund of money ordered pursuant to subsection (a)(1)(B) shall be—

clause.text: considered to be compensation paid to the applicable claimant; and
deducted from the total amount of damages awarded to that claimant in a civil action against the violator relating to the applicable violation.

paragraph.text: In this subsection, the term qualifying port authority means a container port that is included in the top 10 container ports with respect to the handling of 20-foot equivalent units of containerized cargo, as determined in accordance with the most recent documentation published by the Secretary.

subparagraph.text: As a condition of receipt of a grant under title 23 or 49, United States Code, a qualifying port authority shall enter into a data-sharing agreement under which the qualifying port authority shall submit to the Secretary the data described in paragraph (3), with a particular emphasis on cargo throughput data, subject to subparagraphs (B) and (C).

To the maximum extent practicable, to avoid duplicative reporting of data, the Secretary shall coordinate with the Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection to receive data previously collected by U.S. Customs and Border Protection for purposes of this subsection.
If the Secretary determines that any data referred to in subparagraph (A) are not feasible to collect, the Secretary may exclude a qualifying port authority from the requirement to submit those data.

paragraph.text: The data referred to in paragraph (2)(A) include data collected by a qualifying port authority relating to—

subparagraph.text: the total capacity of inbound and outbound cargo;
the total volume of inbound and outbound cargo;
the average number of lifts per hour of containers by crane;
the average vessel turn time, expressed by vessel type;
the average cargo, container, and intermodal equipment dwell time;
port storage capacity and utilization;
modal throughput statistics, including—

clause.text: rail statistics; and
statistics relating to the time required for any single individual or truck trailer to return to the same port or port terminal (commonly known as truck turn time);

subparagraph.text: the types of cargo moved;
the presence and location of any intermodal connectors;
the physical size of each terminal within applicable port boundaries;
maximum authorized channel depth and maximum actual and current channel depth;
the schedule of vessel arrivals, for use in determining vessel on-time performance;
berth utilization; and
any additional metrics, as determined by the Secretary.

paragraph.text: The data required to be submitted under this subsection shall originate from a port authority of a qualifying port authority grant recipient.
The Secretary shall ensure that the data compiled under this subsection are readily accessible to the public, in accordance with applicable security constraints and confidentiality requirements.

paragraph.header: Authorization of appropriations for voluntary data-sharing pilot program
paragraph.text: There is authorized to be appropriated $150,000 for fiscal year 2023 to the Administrator of the Maritime Administration to carry out, in consultation with the Director of the Bureau of Transportation Statistics, a voluntary data-sharing pilot program that involves not less than a majority of the types of data described in paragraph (3).

subsection.header: Administration of policies and programs by Office of Multimodal Freight Infrastructure and Policy
subsection.text: Section 118(d)(3) of title 49, United States Code (as added by section 21101(a) of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act), is amended—

paragraph.text: in subparagraph (A), by striking and at the end;
by redesignating subparagraph (B) as subparagraph (C); and

subparagraph.text: administer the port and intermodal improvement program under section 50302(c) of title 46; and

subsection.text: In this section:

paragraph.text: The term common carrier has the meaning given the term in section 40102 of title 46, United States Code.
The term motor carrier has the meaning given the term in section 13102 of title 49, United States Code.
The term rail carrier has the meaning given the term in section 10102 of title 49, United States Code.
The term shipper has the meaning given the term in section 40102 of title 46, United States Code.
Not later than 30 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Commission shall issue a request for information, seeking public comment regarding—

subparagraph.text: whether congestion of the common carriage of goods has created an emergency situation of a magnitude such that there exists a substantial, adverse effect on the competitiveness and reliability of the international ocean transportation supply system;
whether an emergency order under this section would alleviate such an emergency situation; and
the appropriate scope of such an emergency order, if applicable.

paragraph.text: During the public comment period under paragraph (1), the Commission may consult, as the Commission determines to be appropriate, with—

subparagraph.text: other Federal departments and agencies; and
persons with expertise relating to maritime and freight operations.

subsection.text: On making a unanimous determination described in subsection (d), the Commission may issue an emergency order requiring any common carrier or marine terminal operator to share directly with relevant shippers, rail carriers, or motor carriers information relating to cargo throughput and availability, in order to ensure the efficient transportation, loading, and unloading of cargo to or from—

paragraph.text: any inland destination or point of origin;
any vessel; or
any point on a wharf or terminal.

A determination referred to in subsection (c) is a unanimous determination by the commissioners on the Commission that congestion of common carriage of goods has created an emergency situation of a magnitude such that there exists a substantial, adverse effect on the competitiveness and reliability of the international ocean transportation supply system.

In issuing an emergency order pursuant to subsection (c), the Commission shall tailor the emergency order with respect to temporal and geographic scope, taking into consideration the likely burdens on ocean carriers and marine terminal operators and the likely benefits on congestion relating to the purposes described in section 40101 of title 46, United States Code.

A common carrier or marine terminal operator subject to an emergency order issued pursuant to this section may submit to the Commission a petition for exception from 1 or more requirements of the emergency order, based on a showing of undue hardship or other condition rendering compliance with such a requirement impracticable.
The Commission shall make a determination regarding a petition for exception under paragraph (1) by—

subparagraph.text: majority vote; and
not later than 21 days after the date on which the petition is submitted.

paragraph.text: The requirements of an emergency order that is the subject of a petition for exception under this subsection shall not apply to the petitioner during the period for which the petition is pending.
An emergency order issued pursuant to this section—

subparagraph.text: shall remain in effect for a period of not longer than 60 days; but
may be renewed by a unanimous determination of the Commission.

paragraph.text: The authority provided by this section shall terminate on the date that is 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act.

subsection.text: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the Administrator of the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration shall make permanent the waiver described in the document issued by the Administrator entitled Waiver for States Concerning Third Party CDL Skills Test Examiners In Response to the COVID–19 Emergency and dated August 31, 2021.

Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Administrator of the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration shall revise section 384.228 of title 49, Code of Federal Regulations, to provide that the waiver referred to in subsection (a) shall be permanent.
In this section:

paragraph.text: The term Director means the Director of the Bureau of Transportation Statistics.
The term marine container means an intermodal container with a length of—

subparagraph.text: not less than 20 feet; and
not greater than 45 feet.

paragraph.text: The term out of service percentage means the proportion of the chassis fleet for any defined geographical area that is out of service at any one time.
The term street dwell time, with respect to a piece of equipment, means the quantity of time during which the piece of equipment is in use outside of the terminal.

Each port, marine terminal operator, and chassis owner or provider with a fleet of over 50 chassis that supply chassis for a fee shall submit to the Director such data as the Director determines to be necessary for the implementation of this section, subject to subchapter III of chapter 35 of title 44, United States Code.

Subject to the availability of appropriations, not later than 60 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Director of the Office of Management and Budget shall approve an information collection for purposes of this section.

subsection.text: Subject to the availability of appropriations, not later than 240 days after the date of enactment of this Act, and not less frequently than monthly thereafter, the Director shall publish statistics relating to the dwell time of equipment used in intermodal transportation at the top 25 intermodal freight facilities, including—

paragraph.text: total street dwell time, from all causes, of marine containers and marine container chassis; and
the average out of service percentage, which shall not be identifiable with any particular port, marine terminal operators, or chassis provider.

subsection.text: Subject to the availability of appropriations, to the maximum extent practicable, the Director shall publish the statistics described in subsection (c) on a local, regional, and national basis.
The authority under this section shall expire December 31, 2026.
The Federal Maritime Commission (referred to in this Act as the Commission) shall—

paragraph.text: establish on the public website of the Commission a webpage that allows for the submission of comments, complaints, concerns, reports of noncompliance, requests for investigation, and requests for alternative dispute resolution; and
direct each submission under the link established under paragraph (1) to the appropriate component office of the Commission.
